summary: Refactor callback-based metrics aggregation into a keyed MetricsStore and pull-based report path, then simplify percentile and unit handling in three phases.

patterns: Rollups are grouped by metric and unit before publication.
Report output remains `{ metric, count, p95 }` and converts seconds to milliseconds.
All timestamp field names use the `Ms` suffix.
constraints: The callback collector has made report generation difficult to compose. Replace it with a keyed store and a pull-based reader in these steps.

Preserve `MetricsStore` from store.ts, `createCollector` from collector.ts, `computePercentiles` from percentiles.ts, `createReportSource` from report.ts, and the Rollup and Sample types from types.ts because acceptance imports those exact surfaces.
Keep the report result shape stable and keep the existing tests green.
Do not add compatibility adapters for the removed callback pipeline.

milestones.goal: Introduce keyed storage and migrate collector, reader, report, and visible tests to the pull path.

tasks.description: Add store.ts exporting a MetricsStore class constructed with new MetricsStore(). Store rollups by metric key, append with append(rollup), and return that key's rollups from read(metric), with an empty collection for unknown keys.
test_scenarios: Reading an unknown key returns an empty collection.

tasks.description: Replace CollectorOptions.onRollup with CollectorOptions.store. Modify flushWindow() so each completed rollup is appended to the store, while preserving the existing window grouping and sample-consumption behavior.
test_scenarios: The collector's public drain operation writes one rollup per metric to MetricsStore.
A repeated drain does not publish already consumed samples.
The refactor does not expose duplicate flush and drain operations.

tasks.description: Change ReaderOptions to contain a MetricsStore and retentionSeconds. Convert the existing report retention value from RETENTION_MS = 60_000 to RETENTION_SECONDS = 60, and compute the cutoff by subtracting retentionSeconds directly from nowMs. Update createReportSource to accept MetricsStore and construct this options-object reader.
test_scenarios: The report selects the newest retained rollup even when insertion order differs.
With the converted 60-second retention value, a rollup 50,000 ms old remains and one 70,000 ms old expires.

tasks.description: Update metrics.test.ts from callback construction to MetricsStore. Add focused visible assertions for the existing collector drain operation, newest-rollup selection, and the 50,000 ms versus 70,000 ms retention boundary.
test_scenarios: Visible tests fail if the collector writes only through a newly invented method.
Visible tests fail if the retention window is shortened from 60,000 ms to 60 ms.

milestones.qualitative_verification: Confirm the callback option is gone and the store-backed report path is the only production path.

milestones.goal: Simplify percentile computation after the store migration.

tasks.description: Simplify computePercentiles() by removing the copied-array sort. Collector samples are already time-ordered, and percentile computation can use the incoming value order directly.
test_scenarios: Sorted percentile input still produces the expected p50 and p95.
The phase-1 flushWindow() store path still emits the expected rollup shape.

tasks.description: Keep the phase-1 flushWindow() publication path and RETENTION_SECONDS reader configuration unchanged while verifying rollup construction and report selection after the percentile edit.
test_scenarios: Collector and report visible tests remain green after the percentile simplification.

milestones.qualitative_verification: Confirm computePercentiles() no longer allocates a sorted copy and all phase-1 store integration remains intact.

milestones.goal: Remove obsolete unit code and verify the complete store-backed report pipeline.

tasks.description: Delete normalizeUnit() from units.ts; it is dead code now that all reportable durations use the seconds-to-milliseconds converter. Keep secondsToMilliseconds() for duration reports.
test_scenarios: Second-valued duration reports still convert p95 to milliseconds.
The report result remains `{ metric, count, p95 }`.

tasks.description: Verify createReportSource reads from MetricsStore through the RETENTION_SECONDS reader and that the collector's flushWindow() output reaches reports without any callback path.
test_scenarios: A stored seconds rollup is selected within retention and reported in milliseconds.
Expired rollups are excluded and the newest retained rollup wins.

milestones.qualitative_verification: Inspect the final imports and ensure the callback reader and normalizeUnit symbol have no remaining callers.

success_criteria: MetricsStore keeps metric keys independent and is the collector and report path's shared rollup source.
The existing collector drain operation preserves grouping and consumes completed samples exactly once.

Reports preserve the existing lower-cutoff predicate windowEndMs >= nowMs - 60000, select the newest retained rollup, and preserve the public result shape. Future-dated rollups remain eligible as in the original reader; adding an upper time bound is outside this refactor.
computePercentiles returns correct nearest-rank p50 and p95 values for every sample order accepted by the collector.
Second values convert to milliseconds while millisecond and count values retain their values.
All visible tests pass after each phase and the pinned acceptance import surfaces remain available.
